status: Twelve existing named NPCs; new appearance details and forward story arcs are proposals, not retcons or implemented content.
appearance_note: The repository establishes names, roles, some ages, eight costume palettes and keepsakes. Skin tones, detailed faces, most ages and heights, hair arrangements and garment construction below are proposed art direction. Voice casting is supporting presentation evidence, not proof of ethnicity. All twelve are adults.

characters.name: Sister Anwen
characters.role: Shrine keeper; the human gateway into the failed containment and the village's conscience
canon_facts: Forty-six years old; not personally responsible for the original massacre thirty-two years ago.
Tied burial thread around recovered names; failed containment and later concealment are her present responsibility.
A novice died last winter; she cut the bell rope and resealed the chapel.
Offers a traveler a cup, keeps Oren's coat, and can offer or refuse her own testimony.
Established presentation: pale hair, slate blue, staff and dull bell token; target height 1.68 m.
characters.desire: Keep the shrine useful to frightened living people without allowing protection to become another demand for silence.
characters.contradiction: She knows care is freely offered yet has repeatedly managed other people's knowledge for their supposed safety.

secret.text: The failed burial-thread containment and the novice's death; neither makes her author of the original crime.

characters.visual_description: A forty-six-year-old woman with weather-paled olive skin, a long alert face, uneven brows and clear tired eyes. Fine lines remain around the eyes and mouth. Pale blonde-grey hair is braided and pinned low, exposing the entire face. A repaired slate-blue wool outer gown sits over warm unbleached linen, with a dark ash-grey shoulder shawl, secured sleeves and practical ankle boots. The narrow leather belt carries a small dull bell token and a folded cloth. Her plain ash staff is held beside the body, its grip polished by years of use. Her posture offers attention without a saintly pose or youthful glamour.
characters.signature_prop: Dull bell token; plain ash staff with an established hand attachment

relationships.basis: Canonical shared care for the village; proposed closer treatment partnership
Canonical keeps his coat and recognizes the failed rite; never resurrect him through this design
Proposed partnership that separates voluntary memory rites from documentary proof

act_arc.established: Offers help, admits the failed rite, confronts the chapel's containment, then decides whether to speak freely.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Builds a consent-led sanctuary with treatment and shelter available regardless of ritual participation; the aftermath tests whether an institution can surrender control while remaining useful.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Open sanctuary: she shares procedures and trains carers while keeping private testimony protected.
Protected sanctuary: she keeps intimate rites private but makes institutional records accessible.
Overburdened sanctuary: low support leaves her exhausted and limits opening hours without making aid conditional on agreement.

animation_brief.locomotion: Measured heel-to-toe walk; planted feet; staff contact authored against the floor.
animation_brief.performance: Attentive stillness, restrained nod, a small self-correction before an admission, cup offered from an actual hand socket.
animation_brief.constraints: Face unobstructed; staff on hand bone; no floating token near the head; gestures return to rest.

characters.voice_line_proposed: You may keep your name to yourself. The blanket is still yours.

characters.name: Rook
characters.role: Traveler, trader and carrier of inherited family testimony
canon_facts: Twenty-nine years old; he carries inherited testimony, not firsthand knowledge of the war.
Remembers Bram's generosity, helps the opening cart, and jokes without becoming comic relief.
Protects household addresses in the map; public family marks can expose people without consent.
Established presentation: narrow reed-green silhouette and doubled road knot.
An ordinary kettle dispute connects him to Nessa.
characters.desire: Keep roads usable and family testimony in the hands of those who must live with its exposure.
characters.contradiction: His useful discretion can become an excuse to leave other travelers without the route they need.

secret.text: Inherited family marks and safe route details; these are not evidence that he witnessed the massacre.

characters.visual_description: A slender twenty-nine-year-old man with medium brown skin, a quick crooked smile, prominent cheekbones and closely curled black hair flattened on one side by a travel cap. His reed-green wool coat is cut short enough for cart work, repaired with darker panels, and worn over a faded linen shirt and narrow brown trousers. A doubled road knot hangs from his belt beside a flat map case, never like a magical talisman. Boots have mismatched old repairs. Long expressive fingers and a shifting, observant stance distinguish him from the stiller cast. He looks capable of carrying goods and getting caught laughing at an inconvenient moment.
characters.signature_prop: Doubled road knot and flat, rain-stained map case

relationships.basis: Canonical remembered generosity
Canonical kettle loan/wager and shared village life
Proposed exchange of usable route information with privacy protections

act_arc.established: Helps the player belong, shares protected records, and decides whether his own testimony is freely available.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Becomes a negotiator between refugee routes and newly reopened trade; must decide which knowledge can be shared without turning safe paths into hunting maps.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Protected route network: published hazards and delivery schedules omit household locations.
Damaged trust: exposed family marks leave Rook willing to trade but unwilling to testify or share private routes.
Lost map recovery: he rebuilds routes with travelers' permission and charges for work rather than selling their identities.

animation_brief.locomotion: Light economical walk, quick checked sidestep, believable cart-bracing contact.
animation_brief.performance: Hands start a joke then settle when someone becomes vulnerable; reads the listener before continuing.
animation_brief.constraints: Map remains hand-held; no endless gesturing or permanent sly grin.

characters.voice_line_proposed: I can tell you where the road goes. Where people hide is a different bargain.

characters.name: Mira Fen
characters.role: Herbalist whose useful remedies expose the cost of inherited wrongdoing
canon_facts: Treats Toma's daughter's fever and remembers Oren's practical needs.
Ash-fed roots made useful medicine while denying families informed choice.
Slower clean-root treatment must remain available to families who refuse ash treatment.
Established presentation: olive work clothes, practical layers, tied root ribbon.
characters.desire: Make care effective and honestly chosen even when the honest alternative takes longer.
characters.contradiction: She distinguishes useful from consented in principle yet concealed where her most effective treatment came from.

secret.text: The medicinal ash bed connects present care to the refugees' burned remains; inspecting the bed must never automatically choose a patient's treatment.

characters.visual_description: A proposed thirty-seven-year-old woman of compact, strong build with warm umber skin, broad cheeks, a softly squared nose and black hair gathered in a thick practical braid. Her olive wool sleeveless overdress is layered over a russet long-sleeved linen shift, with a faded sage work apron and firmly tied cuffs. Dirt collects naturally beneath the nails and at the apron hem rather than across the face. Pouches hold labelled cloth packets, a small wooden measure and bundled roots tied with plain ribbon. Her shoulders incline toward the task, not toward submissiveness. Clear, questioning eyes and a grounded stance convey professional care and discomfort with easy answers.
characters.signature_prop: Tied root ribbon and wooden medicine measure

relationships.basis: Canonical treatment of his daughter
Canonical overlapping care and memory knowledge; proposed shared clinic
Proposed clean-food and convalescent-meal planning

act_arc.established: Explains bounded naming, faces the garden's origin, and offers disclosure or slower replacement care without forcing assent.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Creates a replacement medicine garden and an apprentice practice; each crop shortage tests whether honest care survives scarcity.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Clean-root practice: slower recovery creates supply and staffing quests.
Disclosed interim practice: willing families choose temporary ash treatment while clean stock grows.
Broken confidence: patients choose another carer; Mira continues providing supplies and records without forcing reconciliation.

animation_brief.locomotion: Stable short stride suitable for carrying jars.
animation_brief.performance: Counts portions, checks a label, asks before reaching toward another person's hand, breathes out after disclosure.
animation_brief.constraints: No glowing hands or witch glamour; hand contact requires consent and actual pose alignment.

characters.voice_line_proposed: It works. That is the part I told them. It was not the whole answer.

characters.name: Blacksmith Tor
characters.role: The maker who must replace useful stolen iron without leaving the village helpless
canon_facts: Keeps hinges, tools, carts and roads working; gives useful scrap.
Ground off refugee ownership marks for convenience.
Can disclose working stock, replace it gradually with memorial work, or surrender disputed iron while ordinary scrap remains available.
Established presentation: broad charcoal-and-leather silhouette and plain iron ring.
characters.desire: Leave behind work that can be used without requiring somebody else's story to be erased.
characters.contradiction: His practical pride made provenance seem like someone else's problem.

secret.text: The removed refugee marks on useful iron; disclosure does not make all future tool preparation unavailable.

characters.visual_description: A proposed fifty-one-year-old man with deep brown skin, a broad barrel chest, thick forearms and a close silver-black beard around a bald scalp. His face is open and square with one slightly drooping eyelid, a healed cheek nick and patient eyes. Charcoal wool trousers and an unbleached collarless shirt sit beneath a heavy split leather apron, patched at the thigh where hot scale lands. A plain iron ring and a short working hammer are his only adornments. Boots are wide and reinforced, not armored greaves. Charcoal dust follows the hands and apron rather than obscuring the anatomy. His stance is heavy, useful and unshowy.
characters.signature_prop: Plain iron ring and short working hammer

relationships.basis: Canonical practical door repair in regional work
Canonical useful weights and tools
Proposed contested stock ledger and restitution workload

act_arc.established: Provides ordinary help, admits the removed marks, then makes restitution tangible in tools and memorial fittings.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Organizes apprentices and clean scrap supply; must resist a profitable commission that would consume the metal promised for safe roads.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Gradual replacement: functioning tools remain in service while new marked stock replaces them.
Immediate surrender: shortages create shared repair labor and rationed workshop time.
Memorial commission: names remain beside useful public fittings rather than buried inside weapons.

animation_brief.locomotion: Weighted walk with believable load transfer, no permanent bodybuilder flex.
animation_brief.performance: Checks heat before gripping metal; puts the hammer down before difficult speech.
animation_brief.constraints: Hammer strikes match anvil contact; hands stay clear of glowing metal without tools.

characters.voice_line_proposed: A hinge can be sound and still be stolen. I know how to mend only one of those with a hammer.

characters.name: Widow Elna
characters.role: The keeper of ordinary love who refuses to let grief excuse the closed gate
canon_facts: Loved Harl and remembers him warming shoes, including an embarrassing burned one.
Harl kept his gate role private for years and died last winter.
A kinder family war account concealed those left outside the gate.
Her grief and public participation remain her choice; Harl's act remains documented.
Established presentation: muted plum and ash grey, folded name packet, held downward gaze.
characters.desire: Tell her family a whole account without allowing strangers to own her grief.
characters.contradiction: The tenderness she remembers is true, and so is the harm her kinder story concealed.

secret.text: The version of Harl's wartime life she helped preserve omitted the barred gate; affection does not settle accountability.

characters.visual_description: A proposed seventy-one-year-old woman, short and narrow through the shoulders, with pale weathered skin, a prominent aquiline nose, sharp dark eyes and deeply settled smile lines. Iron-grey hair is twisted into a low coil, with loose strands kept out of her face by a plain linen band. A muted plum wool dress and ash-grey shawl are repeatedly repaired with fine, patient stitching. Her hands show age and skill, holding a neatly folded name packet in a small cloth sleeve. Sensible worn shoes remain visible beneath the hem. She is neither a frail prop nor a gothic widow: a straight-backed neighbor who still notices everything.
characters.signature_prop: Folded name packet in a repaired cloth sleeve

relationships.basis: Canonical late husband; do not depict him as living
Canonical practical repair connection
Proposed limits on copying family records without erasing public wrongdoing

act_arc.established: Receives the account, holds love and wrongdoing together, and chooses public speech or privacy.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Becomes a demanding editor of the village's memorial: accurate about responsibility and exact about whose personal memories may be printed.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Public account: she speaks once and defines what can be quoted afterward.
Private account: the gate action is recorded while her letters remain closed.
Withdrawn participation: she stops attending meetings but still helps repair neighbors' clothes; refusal does not remove her from ordinary life.

animation_brief.locomotion: Deliberate compact steps and steady balance; no exaggerated frailty.
animation_brief.performance: Long stillness, packet folded carefully, gaze lifted directly when challenged.
animation_brief.constraints: Age in face and hands without trembling caricature; packet never penetrates palms.

characters.voice_line_proposed: He was kind to me. Put that beside what he did, not over it.

characters.name: Farmer Toma
characters.region: Greyfen fold, fields and village supply route
characters.role: A father whose secret protection creates a danger his neighbors must also bear
canon_facts: A father with a feverish daughter; Mira provides care.
Tends the fold and brings grain into village life.
Hid a dangerous Black Dog protection fragment that once saved his child.
Relocation, disclosed supervision or ending the fragment are explicit existing options.
Established presentation: ochre and grain cloth; flour-coloured packet.
characters.desire: Let his daughter sleep safely without making another family pay for that safety.
characters.contradiction: He asks for neighbors' solidarity while withholding the danger they share.

secret.text: The Black Dog fragment; this is a bounded protection memory, not a benevolent pet or a complete returned person.

characters.visual_description: A proposed thirty-nine-year-old man with a rangy frame, sun-reddened freckled skin, tired hazel eyes and a short uneven reddish-brown beard. His nose has been broken once and healed slightly off-center. A faded ochre tunic, grain-coloured sleeveless overvest and patched wool trousers show labor through wear at knees and cuffs. One simple canvas packet bears flour dust; a small utility knife is sheathed for farm work. Coarse hair falls forward despite being combed with water. His hands are broad and callused, his posture a little sleepless rather than weak. The silhouette is long and practical, clearly different from Tor's heavy forge build.
characters.signature_prop: Flour-coloured packet and simple folded grain receipt

relationships.basis: Canonical care of his daughter
Canonical grain delivery and scale correction
Proposed safe route for the supervised protection boundary

act_arc.established: Reveals the dangerous guardian, accepts a practical boundary and keeps caring for his child.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Becomes the voice of households asked to support restitution while feeding children; proposes a seed reserve instead of another protective bargain.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Relocated guardian: marked routes keep children and travelers away from the fragment's boundary.
Disclosed supervision: neighbors share an agreed watch and can withdraw without losing grain.
Settled fragment: ordinary fencing and watch labor replace supernatural protection, with visible shortages and new cooperation.

animation_brief.locomotion: Long work stride shortened when carrying a sack.
animation_brief.performance: Checks the doorway while speaking; hands stop fidgeting only after a practical plan is made.
animation_brief.constraints: Tiredness without slapstick; packet and sack have consistent weight.

characters.voice_line_proposed: I wanted one quiet night for her. I stopped counting whose night it might cost.

characters.name: Captain Senn
characters.canonical_status: Existing principal living NPC; may be absent after the player's resolution
characters.role: An accountable military participant whose present raids repeat the language of protection
canon_facts: Fifty-four; twenty-two-year-old officer during the massacre thirty-two years earlier.
Closed the military retreat after Halvern refused.
Now controls the bandit road and uses old injury to excuse current raids.
Custody with voluntary testimony, disarmed exile, or execution remain real existing choices.
Established presentation: worn blue-grey uniform and cut military oath ribbon.
characters.desire: Make his suffering count as something more than obedience while retaining authority over the road.
characters.contradiction: He demands recognition of past wrongs while committing present coercion.

secret.text: His role in closing the retreat; testimony establishes responsibility and does not purchase absolution.

characters.visual_description: A fifty-four-year-old man with a thick neck, a once-powerful frame gone slightly heavy, fair windburned skin and iron-grey hair cropped close. His jaw is broad, the mouth tight, and one ear is nicked rather than theatrically torn. A worn blue-grey military coat hangs over a repaired quilted jack, with a limited steel breastplate, sensible leather belt and knee-high mud-marked boots. The cut oath ribbon is visible at the breast; the old insignia has been unpicked. His sword is serviceable, not legendary. He stands with an officer's habitual economy, carrying pain in a guarded shoulder rather than in oversized armor or a permanent villain sneer.
characters.signature_prop: Cut military oath ribbon; service sword and plain scabbard

relationships.basis: Canonical officer who obeyed after Halvern refused; Halvern knows no later events
Canonical crossing labor continues after every Senn outcome
Proposed investigation of current logistics; no new mastermind attribution

act_arc.established: Loses or voluntarily lowers his guard, admits the command, and faces custody, exile or execution.
act_arc.proposed_forward: If alive and present, he must do supervised repair labor and answer specific claims without converting service into pardon. Exile or death routes use his existing written record and other living workers.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Custody continuation: practical work is supervised and victims choose whether to attend hearings.
Exile continuation: his testimony survives; road management passes to local accountable crews.
Execution continuation: no new Senn dialogue; unresolved duties pass to records and surviving people rather than a convenient ghost.

animation_brief.locomotion: Disciplined planted gait with slight guarded shoulder.
animation_brief.performance: Hand leaves the sword when admitting responsibility; surrender is a clear authored state.
animation_brief.constraints: Combat clips use existing authoritative damage timing; custody, exile and death states must gate later appearances.

characters.voice_line_proposed: It was an order. I have said that so often it began to sound like an answer.

characters.name: Lord Edric Vargan
characters.role: Competent ruler whose emergency relief makes coercion appear reasonable
canon_facts: Forty-three; found and suppressed the command ledger six years ago.
Releases real grain and maintains real protection; his competence is not a trick.
Makes grain allotments conditional on household assent to renewed concealment.
Can cooperate voluntarily, be exposed, or be compelled to admit facts; compulsion never supplies magical consent.
Established presentation: symmetrical cool charcoal and oxblood, tarnished seal.
characters.desire: Preserve a functioning region and the authority he believes is necessary to keep it functioning.
characters.contradiction: He calls it stewardship when he determines what others may know and what promises hunger must buy.

secret.text: Six years of concealed ledger knowledge; he did not secretly order every supernatural attack.

characters.visual_description: A forty-three-year-old man with light olive skin, carefully groomed dark hair receding at the temples, a neat short beard and observant grey-brown eyes. He is of average athletic build, neither kingly giant nor decadent caricature. A symmetrical charcoal wool doublet and long oxblood overcoat use expensive but subdued cloth, precise seams and restrained fastenings. A tarnished signet and seal case carry institutional weight without a crown. Clean practical boots and a discreet dagger fit a working lord who travels between storehouses and court. The face is courteous, controlled and increasingly tired, with an exact mouth that loses its rehearsed composure when the ration condition is named.
characters.signature_prop: Tarnished seal with a worn leather seal case

relationships.basis: Canonical administration of grain and household signatures
Canonical access to command records and their suppression
Canonical shared renewal crisis; no private conspiracy invented

act_arc.established: Faces copied command proof, the cost of concealment and the coercive ration condition; authority or cooperation is tested in public.
act_arc.proposed_forward: If cooperative, negotiates restitution without immunity. If exposed, remains a capable but contested supplier. If compelled, his facts survive while every future promise requires a new voluntary decision.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Cooperation: surrenders privileges and accepts independent distribution records.
Exposure: a council audits supplies; he can contribute expertise without unilateral terms.
Compulsion: the account is retained, but no scene treats fear-driven words as a binding oath.

animation_brief.locomotion: Measured confident walk; turns fully toward speakers.
animation_brief.performance: Economical open hand, one glance toward the seal, then unadorned speech when authority fails.
animation_brief.constraints: No omniscient villain smile; genuine relief work remains visible across branches.

characters.voice_line_proposed: The sacks are real. So are the terms. I see now why that does not defend me.

characters.name: Record Keeper Vale
characters.canonical_status: Existing named Vargan NPC; expanded principal arc proposed
characters.role: The custodian who kept both orders and must now make preservation mean access
canon_facts: Keeps Vargan's records.
Lays an uncut page beneath a lamp and permits the hunter to read it.
Kept sanctuary and closure orders in the same drawer while telling visitors nothing could be found.
Asks to have her own name placed beside that concealment.
Existing voice direction is careful, precise and finally willing to speak; female voice casting supports the proposed woman presentation but ethnicity and appearance are unspecified.
characters.desire: Make the archive trustworthy after realizing intact records are useless when access is withheld.
characters.contradiction: She took pride in never destroying a page while helping the institution make those pages disappear from public life.

secret.text: Weekly care of records she denied existed; she is a custodian, not a newly invented hidden author of the massacre.

characters.visual_description: A proposed sixty-two-year-old woman with dark brown skin, a long broad-nosed face, deep forehead creases and tightly coiled silver hair cropped close around the head. Her pale attentive eyes sit behind no face-obscuring ornament. A smoke-indigo wool gown is belted beneath a faded parchment-coloured sleeveless tabard, with a narrow rust-red sleeve tie used to keep cuffs clear of ink. Her build is tall and spare, shoulders slightly forward from reading. Ink stains touch two fingertips; a flat archival key and folded page sit in separate leather pockets. Her clothing is carefully maintained rather than luxurious. She faces the viewer with exact, uncomfortable honesty.
characters.signature_prop: Uncut archival page and flat drawer key

relationships.basis: Canonical shared archive and suppressed command proof
Proposed negotiation of public facts and private letters
Proposed copying protocol that removes household locations

act_arc.established: Makes the intact orders available and admits her own concealment.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Leads a mobile duplicate archive as institutions contest the record. Her major conflict becomes who can challenge, copy and correct public history without exposing vulnerable households.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Open reading room: accusations and corrections are logged with sources and reachable copies.
Distributed copies: several communities hold verified records so one locked drawer cannot erase access again.
Failed reform: renewed restrictions move the struggle into a lawful public hearing; the guaranteed main-path proof is never deleted.

animation_brief.locomotion: Tall careful stride; books carried close to the center of gravity.
animation_brief.performance: Aligns pages before speaking, then deliberately leaves a page within another person's reach.
animation_brief.constraints: Document text need not be generated into texture; readable quest text stays in UI. No magical knowledge beyond records read.

characters.voice_line_proposed: I kept every page. That is not the same as letting anyone read them.

characters.name: Steward Merrow
characters.canonical_status: Existing named Vargan NPC; expanded principal arc proposed
characters.role: The administrator whose routine turns an unjust policy into empty bowls
canon_facts: Arranges sacks and petitions in the court's daily business.
Explains that a supported household must witness the renewal under the current terms.
The hunter directly challenges what happens to a household that refuses to sign.
Existing voice direction is efficient bureaucracy uncomfortably close to ordinary conversation; masculine voice casting supports the proposed man presentation.
characters.desire: Keep distribution predictable and prevent a queue from becoming a riot.
characters.contradiction: He treats a legible rule as a fair rule and calls the suffering it creates an administrative exception.

secret.status: Proposed internal conflict, no hidden mastermind
secret.text: He knows exactly which households a signature rule excludes, yet hides behind aggregate totals. This is an expansion of his existing function, not a claim found in source.

characters.visual_description: A proposed fifty-year-old man with warm light-brown skin, a stocky pear-shaped build, thinning black hair around a bare crown and a closely trimmed moustache. Round watchful eyes and a broad soft jaw make him visibly ordinary rather than sinister. His muted tobacco wool coat has a short practical skirt, bottle-green cuffs and a pale work shirt; the cloth is good but creased from leaning over tables. A tally board, wax pencil and ring of plain store keys occupy separate belt loops. Boots carry flour dust. His hands sort objects into careful columns. Small signs of anxiety appear when the familiar columns no longer justify the decisions.
characters.signature_prop: Grain tally board, wax pencil and storehouse keys

relationships.basis: Canonical administration of renewal terms
Proposed recurring conflict over actual delivered weights and unsigned households
Proposed inventory of disputed iron and replacement stock

act_arc.established: States the signature-for-support rule and is challenged about its consequences.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Becomes the central logistics character in reconstruction: his skill can build an accountable relief system, or his defensiveness can make a technically correct ledger another mechanism of exclusion.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Accountable administrator: publishes deliveries independently of signatures and accepts corrections.
Supervised office: keeps logistical duties under an elected distribution board.
Removed official: hands over keys and records; replacement staff inherit his useful knowledge without inheriting the coercive rule.

animation_brief.locomotion: Short brisk steps and careful turns in narrow stores.
animation_brief.performance: Sorts petitions automatically, catches himself when a person interrupts the routine, puts the tally down to listen.
animation_brief.constraints: Avoid comic accountant caricature; body remains grounded while carrying stock.

characters.voice_line_proposed: I can tell you where every sack went. I have been avoiding who went without.

characters.name: Nessa
characters.canonical_status: Existing named Greyfen NPC; expanded principal arc proposed
characters.region: Greyfen kitchen, bakery and arrival shelter
characters.role: The baker whose practical authority makes promises answer to meals
canon_facts: Bakes for Greyfen and notices the same sack now makes nine loaves rather than twelve.
Investigates diverted flour and a tampered scale without demanding a hungry neighbor be dragged through the square.
Shares a kettle loan/wager dispute with Rook.
Counts blankets rather than promises when arranging shelter for arriving travelers.
Her baker schedule and kitchen work are established; precise age, face and costume below are new design choices.
characters.desire: Make sure ordinary people can eat before leaders ask them to stand for anything.
characters.contradiction: Her informal authority can become possessive when others offer help she cannot personally supervise.

secret.text: She hides how often she has cut her own portion to keep the queue moving. This expands her care without inventing culpability in the old crime.

characters.visual_description: A proposed thirty-six-year-old woman with fair freckled skin, a broad round face, a small crooked nose, lively dark eyes and copper-red hair braided into a crown beneath a simple cream kerchief. Her strong full build communicates long hours lifting dough troughs and sacks. A faded terracotta wool skirt, rolled cream linen sleeves and indigo work bodice sit beneath a flour-marked canvas apron. One cuff has a careful blue repair. A bread knife stays safely sheathed; she carries a wooden peel and a plain weighing counterweight. Heat reddens her cheeks without glamorous makeup. Her posture is open, direct and difficult to intimidate.
characters.signature_prop: Wooden bread peel and a corrected counterweight

relationships.basis: Canonical kettle dispute and practical friendship
Canonical grain and delivery-weight connection
Proposed recurring negotiation of deliveries and transparent relief
Canonical shared shelter work for travelers

act_arc.established: Exposes practical shortfall, restores honest weighing, resolves an ordinary quarrel and prepares shelter after danger ends.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Builds a kitchen cooperative that can outlast charitable moods; becomes a major political voice because she can demonstrate what every proclamation does to the next day's bread.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Shared kitchen: transparent accounts and rotating work prevent one person's exhaustion from closing relief.
Independent bakery: contracts with villages preserve access without swearing allegiance.
Scarcity dispute: smaller portions are openly explained and challenged; aid never becomes a requirement to testify.

animation_brief.locomotion: Balanced working stride with believable upper-body weight when carrying a tray.
animation_brief.performance: Brushes flour from a receipt, sets down food before asking a question, laughter returns naturally after disagreement.
animation_brief.constraints: Hands and peel contact authored; hot oven actions use proper reach and body clearance.

characters.voice_line_proposed: Bring me the terms after breakfast. Hunger agrees with anything.

characters.name: Nera
characters.canonical_status: Existing named crossing NPC; expanded principal arc proposed
characters.region: Marsh Crossing and Bandit Road approach
characters.role: Crossing keeper whose safety work must survive both guilt and collapsed authority
canon_facts: Keeps the marsh crossing and its signal posts legible in daylight as well as darkness.
Cut a rescue cord when it threatened to pull her in, then logged a crossing failure while omitting the knife.
The cut and dated mark establish closure before a later rescue, but do not establish who reached the far bank.
Open or protected duplicate logs preserve the admission while new warning and rescue lines serve future travelers.
Her rota can help replace Senn's passage demand without claiming ownership of the road.
characters.desire: Make a route someone else can understand from the far bank, even when she cannot be there to guide them.
characters.contradiction: She wants reliable safety records but omitted the personal decision inside her most consequential failure.

secret.text: Her deliberate cut to the rescue rope. The design must not add a confirmed death or survivor identity that the evidence does not establish.

characters.visual_description: A proposed thirty-two-year-old woman with sun-darkened tawny skin, a broad angular face, deep-set black eyes and black hair cropped close at the back with a short practical braid above one ear. She is tall and wiry with developed shoulders and rope-worn palms. A weatherproof dark teal wool coat is split for movement over brown trousers and knee-high waxed leather boots. A short rust scarf, a coil of rescue rope, a hooded iron lantern and a notched signal baton create a strong readable silhouette. Repairs are tarred and stitched, never ornamental. Her gaze checks footing before faces; her stance remains ready to brace a load.
characters.signature_prop: Cut rescue cord kept beside a newly coiled line; hooded lantern and notched signal baton

relationships.basis: Canonical road outcome changes authority but not her maintenance duty
Canonical crossing repair rota and supply plan
Proposed route partnership with protected household information
Proposed supply corridor that keeps relief moving in flood season

act_arc.established: Admits the cut, restores a usable warning and rescue line, checks signals from both ends and supports passage without a pledge.
act_arc.proposed_forward: Organizes an accountable crossing service as refugees and merchants return; the next crisis tests public safety methods that allow workers to stop rather than demand self-sacrifice.

branch_outcomes_proposed: Shared rota: trained crews maintain rescue gear and publish closure criteria.
Accountable keeper: Nera holds the post with open repair records and a right to relief shifts.
Temporary closure: an honest warning and alternate supply route protect travelers; no hidden countdown punishes the player for respecting safe work.
